units.title: Sequence and Series
units.intro: A **sequence** is a list $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$. A **series** is the sum $S_n=a_1+\cdots+a_n$.

cards.title: 1.1 Basic Ideas of Sequence
body: For each of the sequences in task (3) try to find a general formula that describes the given sequence.
A sequence in mathematics is a function whose domain is the set of positive integers.
If the domain consists of the first “n” positive integers only, then the sequence is a finite sequence.
Remark: The general formula of a sequence is also known as the nth term formula of the sequence.
For n a natural number n, nfactorial, denoted by n! is the product of the first n natural numbers.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What are the first five terms of the sequence given by the explicit formula $$a_n = 4n - 1$$?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Understand the given formula**
We are given the explicit formula $$a_n = 4n - 1$$ for $$n \ge 1$$.

**Step 2: Calculate the terms systematically**
For $$n = 1$$: $$a_1 = 4(1) - 1 = 3$$
For $$n = 2$$: $$a_2 = 4(2) - 1 = 7$$
For $$n = 3$$: $$a_3 = 4(3) - 1 = 11$$
For $$n = 4$$: $$a_4 = 4(4) - 1 = 15$$
For $$n = 5$$: $$a_5 = 4(5) - 1 = 19$$

**Step 3: Combine the results**
The first five terms are **$$3, 7, 11, 15, 19$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Find the $$7^{\text{th}}$$ term of the sequence given by $$a_n = (-1)^n(2n + 3)$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify the given values**
We need to find the term for $$n = 7$$ in the formula $$a_n = (-1)^n(2n + 3)$$.

**Step 2: Substitute $$n = 7$$**
$$a_7 = (-1)^7(2(7) + 3)$$

**Step 3: Compute the expression**
$$a_7 = (-1) \times (14 + 3)$$
$$a_7 = -17$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The seventh term is **$$-17$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Find the next three terms of the sequence: $$8, 5, 2, -1, -4, \dots$$
cards.why:
**Step 1: Determine the pattern of the sequence**
Observe the difference between consecutive terms:
$$5 - 8 = -3$$
$$2 - 5 = -3$$
$$-1 - 2 = -3$$
Since the difference is constant, this is an AP with first term $$a_1 = 8$$ and common difference $$d = -3$$.

**Step 2: Calculate the next three terms**
The last given term is $$-4$$.
Term 6: $$-4 + (-3) = -7$$
Term 7: $$-7 + (-3) = -10$$
Term 8: $$-10 + (-3) = -13$$

**Step 3: Conclude**
The next three terms are **$$-7, -10, -13$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Simplify the algebraic factorial expression: $$\frac{(n+1)!}{n!}$$ where $$n$$ is a positive integer.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Write down the definition of factorial**
By definition, $$(n+1)! = (n+1) \times n \times (n-1) \times \dots \times 1 = (n+1) \times n!$$.

**Step 2: Substitute this expression into the fraction**
$$\frac{(n+1)!}{n!} = \frac{(n+1) \times n!}{n!}$$

**Step 3: Simplify by canceling out the common terms**
Cancel the common term $$n!$$ from numerator and denominator to get $$n + 1$$.

**Step 4: Final Result**
The simplified expression is **$$n + 1$$**.

cards.title: 1.2 Arithmetic Progression
body: An **arithmetic progression (AP)** is a sequence in which each term is obtained from the previous one by adding the same number, the **common difference** d = aₙ₊₁ − aₙ.
**General term:** aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d. **Sum of the first n terms:** Sₙ = n/2 · (2a₁ + (n − 1)d) = n/2 · (a₁ + aₙ).
**Arithmetic mean:** if a, b, c are in AP then b = (a + c)/2. Inserting k arithmetic means between a and b gives an AP with k + 2 terms, so d = (b − a)/(k + 1).

**Example (business):** a business makes a profit of 10,000 Nakfa in its first year and the profit grows by 2,500 Nakfa each year. Profit in year 6: a₆ = 10,000 + 5 × 2,500 = 22,500 Nakfa. Total profit in 6 years: S₆ = 6/2 × (10,000 + 22,500) = 97,500 Nakfa.
**Testing for an AP:** compute the differences between consecutive terms; the sequence is an AP only if they are all equal. 3, 7, 11, 15 (d = 4) is an AP; 1, 4, 9, 16 is not.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Determine whether the sequence $$3, 7, 11, 15, 19, \dots$$ is an Arithmetic Progression, and find its common difference $$d$$.

options.C: No, it is not an AP

cards.why:
**Step 1: Check the difference between consecutive terms**
Calculate $$a_n - a_{n-1}$$ for all consecutive terms:
$$7 - 3 = 4$$
$$11 - 7 = 4$$
$$15 - 11 = 4$$
$$19 - 15 = 4$$

**Step 2: Formulate the conclusion**
Since the difference is a constant value of $$4$$, the sequence is indeed an Arithmetic Progression.

**Step 3: Final Result**
It is an AP with common difference **$$d = 4$$**.

cards.why:
**Step 1: State the formula for the Arithmetic Mean**
For any two numbers $$a$$ and $$b$$, the Arithmetic Mean $$x$$ is given by:
$$x = \frac{a + b}{2}$$

**Step 2: Substitute the given values**
Substitute $$a = 3.5$$ and $$b = 7$$:
$$x = \frac{3.5 + 7}{2}$$

**Step 3: Perform the calculations**
$$x = \frac{10.5}{2} = 5.25$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The Arithmetic Mean is **$$5.25$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Calculate the sum of the first 10 terms ($$S_{10}$$) of an Arithmetic Progression where $$A_1 = 7$$ and $$d = 2$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: State the arithmetic series sum formula**
The formula is $$S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a_1 + (n - 1)d]$$.

**Step 2: Substitute the known values**
Here $$n = 10$$, $$a_1 = 7$$, and $$d = 2$$:
$$S_{10} = \frac{10}{2}[2(7) + (10 - 1)2]$$

**Step 3: Solve inside the bracket**
$$S_{10} = 5[14 + (9)2]$$
$$S_{10} = 5[14 + 18]$$
$$S_{10} = 5[32] = 160$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The sum of the first 10 terms is **$$160$$**.

cards.title: 1.3 Geometric Progression
body: A **geometric progression (GP)** is a sequence where each term is the previous term multiplied by the same non-zero number, the **common ratio** r = aₙ₊₁ / aₙ.
**General term:** aₙ = a₁ rⁿ⁻¹. **Sum of n terms:** Sₙ = a₁(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1) for r ≠ 1 (if r = 1, Sₙ = n a₁).
**Geometric mean:** if a, b, c are in GP then b² = ac, so b = √(ac) for positive a, c.
**Example (growth):** an E. coli cell divides into two every 20 minutes. Starting from 1 cell, after 3 hours there are 9 divisions, so 1 × 2⁹ = 512 cells.
**Example:** in a GP a₂ = 6 and a₅ = 48. Then r³ = 48/6 = 8, so r = 2 and a₁ = 3.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: In a GP, a₁ = 5 and r = 3. What is a₄?
cards.why: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹, so a₄ = 5 × 3³ = 5 × 27 = 135. (14 would come from adding 3 each time — that is an AP.)

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Find the next term of the geometric progression: $$27, 9, 3, 1, \dots$$
cards.why:
**Step 1: Find the common ratio $$r$$**
Calculate the ratio of consecutive terms:
$$r = \frac{g_2}{g_1} = \frac{9}{27} = \frac{1}{3}$$
Let's verify:
$$g_3 = 9 \times \frac{1}{3} = 3$$
$$g_4 = 3 \times \frac{1}{3} = 1$$ (correct).

**Step 2: Find the next term ($$g_5$$)**
Multiply the fourth term by the common ratio:
$$g_5 = g_4 \times r = 1 \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{3}$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
The next term is **$$\frac{1}{3}$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Find the Geometric Mean of the numbers $$3 - \sqrt{5}$$ and $$3 + \sqrt{5}$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Write down the geometric mean formula**
For two numbers $$a$$ and $$b$$, the Geometric Mean $$x$$ is:
$$x = \sqrt{ab}$$

**Step 2: Substitute the given numbers**
$$x = \sqrt{(3 - \sqrt{5})(3 + \sqrt{5})}$$

**Step 3: Simplify inside the radical**
Use the difference of squares identity $$(A-B)(A+B) = A^2 - B^2$$:
$$(3 - \sqrt{5})(3 + \sqrt{5}) = 3^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2 = 9 - 5 = 4$$

**Step 4: Compute the final square root**
$$x = \sqrt{4} = 2$$
The Geometric Mean is **$$2$$**.

cards.title: 1.4 Harmonic Progression
body: A sequence is a **harmonic progression (HP)** if the reciprocals of its terms form an arithmetic progression. Example: 1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, … is an HP because 1, 2, 3, 4, … is an AP.

**To find a term of an HP:** take reciprocals, find the term of the AP, then take the reciprocal again. For 1/2, 1/5, 1/8, …: the AP is 2, 5, 8, … with d = 3, so its 10th term is 2 + 9 × 3 = 29 and the 10th term of the HP is 1/29.
**Harmonic mean** of a and b: H = 2ab/(a + b). For positive a, b the means satisfy AM ≥ GM ≥ HM and AM × HM = GM².
There is no simple formula for the sum of an HP.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: Which sequence is a harmonic progression?
cards.why: Take reciprocals: 3, 6, 9, 12 is an AP (d = 3), so 1/3, 1/6, 1/9, 1/12 is an HP. 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 has reciprocals 2, 4, 8 — a GP, not an AP.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: What is the harmonic mean of 4 and 12?
cards.why: H = 2ab/(a + b) = 2 × 4 × 12/16 = 96/16 = 6. (8 is the arithmetic mean and √48 the geometric mean; note 8 > √48 > 6.)

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Find the Harmonic Mean between the fractions $$\frac{1}{3}$$ and $$\frac{1}{7}$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Recall the definition of Harmonic Progression and Harmonic Mean**
If $$a, m, b$$ form a Harmonic Progression, then $$\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{m}, \frac{1}{b}$$ are in Arithmetic Progression.
Alternatively, the Harmonic Mean $$m$$ is defined as:
$$m = \frac{2ab}{a+b}$$

**Step 2: Substitute $$a = \frac{1}{3}$$ and $$b = \frac{1}{7}$$**
$$m = \frac{2 \times \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{7}}{\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{7}}$$

**Step 3: Simplify the numerator and denominator**
Numerator: $$2 \times \frac{1}{21} = \frac{2}{21}$$
Denominator: $$\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{7} = \frac{7+3}{21} = \frac{10}{21}$$

**Step 4: Solve for $$m$$**
$$m = \frac{\frac{2}{21}}{\frac{10}{21}} = \frac{2}{10} = \frac{1}{5}$$

**Step 5: Final Result**
The Harmonic Mean is **$$\frac{1}{5}$$**.

body: An infinite series whose sum approaches a finite number is called a convergent series.
Find the total distance that the ball travels.
A monument is constructed by first laying a row of 60 bricks at ground level.
A second row with two fewer bricks is centred on that; a third row, with two fewer bricks, is centred on the second; and so on.

cards.title: Arithmetic (AP)
body: Common difference $d=a_{k+1}-a_k$ (constant).
$$a_n=a_1+(n-1)d\qquad S_n=\frac{n}{2}\bigl(2a_1+(n-1)d\bigr)=\frac{n}{2}(a_1+a_n)$$

cards.title: Trick
body: If you know first and last, use $S_n=\frac{n}{2}(a_1+a_n)$ — fewer slips than the $2a_1$ form. To find $n$, solve $a_n=a_1+(n-1)d$ for $n$ and check it is a whole number.

cards.title: Geometric (GP)
body: Common ratio $r=a_{k+1}/a_k$ (constant, $r\neq0$).
$$a_n=a_1 r^{n-1}\qquad S_n=a_1\frac{r^n-1}{r-1}\ (r\neq1)\qquad |r|<1:\ S_\infty=\frac{a_1}{1-r}$$

cards.title: Trick
body: Write the ratio as a fraction, not a rounded decimal, until the last line. For $S_\infty$ first ask: is $|r|<1$? If $|r|\ge 1$ there is no finite infinite sum.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: Find the sum to infinity of 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 + …
cards.why: |r| = 1/2 < 1, so the series converges: S∞ = a₁/(1 − r) = 8/(1/2) = 16.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: For which common ratio does a geometric series converge?
cards.why: An infinite geometric series converges only when |r| < 1. Only −0.5 satisfies this.
